notes:
Summary:
- Mid-market product analytics SaaS. Building guided in-app assistant + enterprise doc-search. Current provider: ProviderX (custom compat layer).
- Goal: migrate to Redwood Hosted for fast time-to-value, then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput & data isolation.
Key asks from Elmcrest:
- Prompt parity with ProviderX (exact or within tolerable delta). CTO: 'We need output parity for core workflows — small wording shifts are OK but benchmarks must pass).'
- Regression detection: automated evals on 12k canonical prompts, token-level diffs, highlight hallucination/capability regressions.
- Compat layer: mapping old API calls -> Redwood tool-calling and stop-sequence semantics; want a short shim so frontend changes are minimal.
- Latency/Throughput: p95 generation < 250ms for short prompts in prod Dedicated; batch reranking throughput 600 rps target for embeddings+rerank path.
- Security: SSO/SAML + audit logging, KMS for keys, data-residency in NA. Legal also asked for retention controls and exportable audit trails.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget expectations; wants Redwood Optimize recommendations to trade quantization vs quality.
POC observations (hosted):
- Token accounting visible in console was a big win for their finance lead.
- Two prompts failed safety parity (more conservative on Redwood hosted); SE note: likely tweakable via model variant + moderation config.
- Streaming behavior: Redwood streams earlier with slightly different chunk boundaries; frontend teams ok if final tokens identical — need canonical diff tooling.
- KV cache test: noticeable 18% cost reduction with prefix caching on one workload during POC weekend.
Communications/snippets:
- Quote (CTO Jon Mayer): 'We won't accept a regression that reduces conversion in onboarding flows. Show us A/B on 50k events.'
- Dev note: 'ProviderX uses special stop tokens; need mapping. Our CI asserts exact match on 80% of golden replies.'
Next steps (short):
- Redwood to deliver Hosted POC parity report by 2026-03-15 (incl. token diffs, safety regressions, suggested model variants).
- Exec pricing sync w/ RevOps on 2026-03-17 to align Dedicated commitment options.
- Legal to receive SSO + audit design doc (Alicia to push link).

Notes style: shorthand bullets, dev quotes, action items.
migration_notes:
Current architecture: ProviderX internal shim -> frontend. Elmcrest wants minimal frontend changes. Migration requests:
- Provide a ProviderX -> Redwood compatibility mapping guide (API endpoints, param mapping, stop token handling, tool-calls).
- Golden prompt parity suite (12k prompts) to run in CI; produce per-prompt similarity score (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic embedding similarity) and flag > 10% delta.
- Safety/regression harness: run hosted responses through Elmcrest internal evals and Redwood's regression alerts (tie to Redwood Optimize).
- Tokenization/cost differences: provide sample tokenization outputs for common locales and languages.
- Plan for dedicated cutover: staged routing (hosted for canary customers, then Dedicated pool for enterprise tenants); fallback to Hosted if Dedicated capacity constrained.
Risks: tokenization differences, moderation alignment, streaming chunk behavior, cost delta on long-context prompts.

- Migration credit for first 3 months Hosted spend to offset dual-run costs.
- Option to convert hosted usage to credit against Dedicated commit within first quarter post-commit.
